A token watermark uses a secret, context-dependent partition of vocabulary into favored and unfavored tokens, then biases generation toward the favored set. A detector counts favored tokens and compares with the null expectation. In a simplified independent null with favored fraction $\gamma$, $z=(G-\gamma T)/\sqrt{T\gamma(1-\gamma)}$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10226)

Real text violates simple independence assumptions, and detection power depends on length, entropy, edits, and the chosen key. Paraphrasing or mixed authorship can reduce the signal; repeated testing needs calibrated thresholds. A positive score is statistical evidence for a particular watermarking mechanism, not proof of authorship or a universal AI-text detector. Validate false positives on relevant human text and protect keys; do not equate missing watermark evidence with human origin.
